questions.q: A sample of $4 . 5mg$ of an unknown monohydric alcohol, $R - OH$ was added to methylmagnesium iodide. A gas is evolved and is collected and its volume measured to be $3 . 1mL$. The molecular weight of the unknown alcohol is $g / mol$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Alcohols on reaction with Grignard reagent forms hydrocarbons.This is due to the presence of active hydrogen in alcohols and here grignard reagent acts as a base.

When any alcohol is treated with methyl magnemsium iodide the hydrocarbon formed should be methane gas.

$ROH + {CH}_{3}MgI \to ROMgI + {CH}_{4} \left(g\right)$

Number of moles of ${CH}_{4} =$ Number of moles of~$ROH$

$⇒ $\dfrac{Volume ( Litres ) ofthegas}{22400} = \dfrac{massofthegas}{Molecularmassofthegas} (Assuming $NTP$ Condition)

$⇒ $\dfrac{3 . 1}{22400} = \dfrac{4 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}}{Molecularmassofthegas}

$⇒ MM = 32 . 51$

$= 33g / mol

$
